turns.question: Where are streaming responses implemented, and which public API methods route into the streaming implementation?
turns.text:
Good, found the core files. Let me examine the key implementation files.Now let's find the public API methods that create these Stream instances — searching for `Stream<` usage and `stream: true` in resources.Now let's check responses.ts and beta/threads/runs.ts stream() convenience methods, plus the lib files.Now let's check assistants/runs.ts stream() and the lib/ files briefly for how they use the core Stream class.Now let's check the higher-level `src/lib` files to understand how they wrap `Stream.fromSSEResponse` / `_client.post`.I have enough evidence now to write the full answer.

## Streaming implementation in `openai-node`

**Core SSE/stream engine:** `src/core/streaming.ts` (canonical location; `src/streaming.ts` just re-exports it and is marked `@deprecated`).

- `export class Stream<Item> implements AsyncIterable<Item>` — the generic wrapper every streaming API method returns.
  - `Stream.fromSSEResponse(response, controller, client?, synthesizeEventData?)` — parses a `text/event-stream` `Response` body into an async iterable of typed events (handles `[DONE]`, JSON-parses each `data:` line, throws `APIError` on `{error: ...}` payloads, and specially handles `thread.*` events for the Assistants API).
  - `Stream.fromReadableStream(readableStream, controller, client?)` — builds a stream from a newline-delimited JSON `ReadableStream` (used when reconstructing a stream client-side, e.g. via `.toReadableStream()`/`.fromReadableStream()` round-tripping, such as forwarding a stream from a Next.js/Express server to a browser).
  - Helper internals: `_iterSSEMessages`, `iterSSEChunks`, `SSEDecoder` (parses raw SSE `event:`/`data:` lines), plus `tee()` and `toReadableStream()` for splitting/serializing.

**Wiring from HTTP layer into `Stream`:** `src/internal/parse.ts`, function `defaultParseResponse`. When request options have `stream: true`, it calls either `props.options.__streamClass.fromSSEResponse(...)` (a custom subclass, if the resource specified one) or falls back to `Stream.fromSSEResponse(...)`. This is invoked from `APIPromise` (`src/core/api-promise.ts`) when the promise is awaited/`.then()`ed — i.e., every resource's `.create()`/`.retrieve()` call returns an `APIPromise`, and if `stream: true` was set in the request options, resolving that promise yields a `Stream<Item>` instead of the parsed JSON body.

## Public API methods that route into it

All of these set `stream: <bool>` on the request passed to `this._client.post/get(...)`, so the return type is `APIPromise<Stream<T>>` when `stream: true`:

| Method | File | Item type |
|---|---|---|
| `client.chat.completions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts` | `Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>` |
| `client.completions.create({stream:true})` (legacy) | `src/resources/completions.ts` | `Stream<Completion>` |
| `client.responses.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts` | `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>` |
| `client.responses.retrieve(id, {stream:true})` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts` | `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.create(threadId, {stream:true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts` | `Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>` |
| `client.beta.threads.createAndRun({stream:true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/threads.ts` | `Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>` |
| `client.images.edit({stream:true})` / `client.images.generate({stream:true})` | `src/resources/images.ts` | `Stream<ImageEditStreamEvent>` / `Stream<ImageGenStreamEvent>` |
| `client.audio.transcriptions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/audio/transcriptions.ts` | `Stream<TranscriptionStreamEvent>` |

**Higher-level convenience wrappers** (in `src/lib/`) build on top of the raw `Stream<T>` above, adding event accumulation/parsing:
- `client.chat.completions.stream(params)` → `ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion` (`src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts`), which internally calls `client.chat.completions.create({...params, stream:true})` and iterates the resulting `Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>`.
- `client.responses.stream(params)` → `ResponseStream.createResponse` (`src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts`), calling `client.responses.create({stream:true})` internally.
- `client.beta.threads.runs.stream(threadId, params)` → `AssistantStream.createAssistantStream` (`src/lib/AssistantStream.ts`), which uses `Stream.fromReadableStream`/the runs `create` call under the hood.
- All three extend `EventStream` (`src/lib/EventStream.ts`), a base class providing `.on(event, cb)`, `.done()`, abort handling, etc.
- `client.chat.completions.runTools(...)` dispatches to `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner` (`src/lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts`) when `body.stream` is set, which is itself built on `ChatCompletionStream`.

**Not part of the SSE `Stream<T>` path** (worth flagging as a different mechanism): `client.audio.speech.create()` (`src/resources/audio/speech.ts`) returns a raw binary `APIPromise<Response>` via `__binaryResponse: true` — it streams audio bytes, not SSE-typed events, so it doesn't go through `core/streaming.ts` at all.

### What I did not verify
- I did not execute or unit-test any of this code — only read source via `gh api`.
- I did not check `src/resources/realtime/*` (WebSocket-based streaming for the Realtime API) in detail; the file listing showed no SSE `Stream<...>` usage there, suggesting it uses a separate WebSocket abstraction, but I didn't inspect `realtime.ts`/`ws.ts`/`ws-base.ts` closely enough to describe its mechanism.
- I didn't check every one of the ~140 resource files for other `stream:` params (e.g. batch or eval endpoints) beyond the ones the `grep` surfaced, though the grep against `Stream<`/`APIPromise<...Stream` across the resources directory should have caught all SSE-based ones.

for f in src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts src/resources/completions.ts src/resources/responses/responses.ts src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts src/resources/beta/threads/threads.ts src/resources/audio/speech.ts src/resources/audio/transcriptions.ts src/resources/realtime/calls.ts src/resources/images.ts src/resources/videos.ts; do
  echo "=== $f ==="
  gh api "repos/openai/openai-node/contents/$f" --jq .content 2>/dev/null | base64 -d | grep -n "Stream<\|APIPromise<.*Stream\|stream(" | head -40
  echo
done
